we have shown that a deep learning based approach to algorithm selection can outperform the state-of-the-art on a variety of problem domains.

1) we propose a novel approach for automatically generating informative features using deep learning, 2) we show that our method is able to achieve state of the art results on multiple problem domains, 3) our approach completely eliminates the need for manually designed features and 4) our approach can be easily applied to new problem domains.
we present a fully automated approach for producing an informative feature set for use in algorithm selection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a methodology to automate the feature engineering process in the context of algorithm selection.
the question of how to automatically construct features that will lead to the best possible performance when selecting an appropriate solver for an instance.
the question, can deep learning be used to automate the algorithm selection pipeline?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented approach is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of problems without the need for manual feature engineering, and can therefore be applied to new problems in a matter of minutes.
the proposed methodology can be utilized in any domain where a large number of solvers exists, and the performance of each solver varies significantly across a wide range problem instances.
our approach is the first to automatically produce a set of algorithm selection features, and the first to produce a set of features which outperform the best solver on a number of problem domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are proposing a novel approach to automatically generate features from problem instances, using Deep Learning techniques.
deep learning can be used as a feature extractor in algorithm portfolio selection.
deep learning is not just for images and natural language processing, it can also be applied to the field of algorithm selection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deep learning approach is able to produce features that are more informative than hand-crafted features.
deep learning techniques can be successfully applied to the problem of automated algorithm selection and that they can be used to automatically generate informative features.

deep learning can provide a general framework for automatically generating informative features, thus enabling the use of algorithm selection techniques in many domains without requiring the manual design of features.
